items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Closures: Anonymous functions that capture variables from their surroundings.
Constructor: __construct initialises each new object; promoted parameters collapse the boilerplate.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Scope: Where a variable is visible: global, local, static and closure scope.
Variables: Named storage for a value; PHP infers the type from what you assign.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Constructor Property Promotion: Declaring constructor parameters as properties in a single step (PHP 8).

8285.title: Now, here’s a version of the Person class that can use a PersonWriter object
8285.code:
<?php
class Person
{
    public function output(PersonWriter $writer): void
    {
        $writer->write($this);
    }
    public function getName(): string
    {
        return "Bob";
    }

    public function getAge(): int
    {
        return 44;
    }
}

8286.title: Anonymous Classes
8286.code:
<?php
$person = new Person();
$person->output(
    new class implements PersonWriter {
        public function write(Person $person): void
        {
            print $person->getName() . " " . $person->getAge() . "\n";
        }
    }
);

8287.title: Let’s create a slightly more complex PersonWriter
8287.code:
<?php
$person = new Person();
$person->output(
    new class ("/tmp/persondump") implements PersonWriter {
        private $path;

        public function __construct(string $path)
        {
            $this->path = $path;
        }

        public function write(Person $person): void
        {
            file_put_contents($this->path, $person->getName() . " " .
             $person->getAge() . "\n");
        }
    }
);
